chapter: Stuff Smith, CBS and radio work
title: Getting a CBS staff job after the radio article
summary: Hall returns from Chicago, reads of a plan to hire Black radio musicians and wins the Mildred Bailey radio band job after a union fuss.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: What was the nature of the article?
Well, that they were going to hire blacks for the media.
So, you came back to New York?
And you did indeed get into the studio?
I hope this won't be too lengthy explaining it.

I was on a record date and we were coming up 7th Avenue and with, Teddy Reig was in the car, well, Teddy Reig was a daily visitor at my house at that point. And we came to a stop light and so he jumped out to get a Metronome mag, which was popular then, and he was reading a column about Mildred Bailey was going to have a radio show with Red Norvo and it mentioned my name.
But nobody had called me, so I called Downbeat, what's the clarinet player's name from Philly?

Buddy DeFranco's girl friend was working at Downbeat, they weren't married yet, and so I called Downbeat to find out about it. So, she called Lou Shoobe (incredible) at CBS, why wasn't I called, and he proclaimed that he couldn't find me, and it became a cause celebre to the union and whatnot,

and I finally got it. So, we had 39 weeks once a week radio show which Roosevelt had claimed radio as an essential industry and it changed my 1-A status to 1-E or something, that you wouldn't be called, so for 39 weeks I was --

Must of been '43 because we were still working when Roosevelt died in '45. There was Ernie Caceres (inaudible) and Will Bradley and Roy and Charlie and Tommy and we had a hell of a band, 32 pieces, and strings. We used to have a ball.
